children: New Delhi, Oct. 29 -- Paras Healthcare shares fell by over 2% in early trade on Thursday, October 29, following a decent stock market debut the day before. However, the stock rebounded sharply, rising 5.4% to a record high of Rs.777 per share on the BSE.
Paras Healthcare share price today opened at an intraday low of Rs.719.75 per share, and touched an intraday high of Rs.777 apiece.

On Wednesday, the stock ended at Rs.737.15 on the BSE, up 6.37% from the issue price. On the NSE, it closed at Rs.735.60, up 6.14%. The stock listed at Rs.720 on the BSE and NSE, a 3.89% premium over its IPO price of Rs.693 per share.
The initial public offering (IPO) of Paras Healthcare was subscribed 2.23 times on the final day of bidding last Friday. The company had set the price band at Rs.660- Rs.693 per share.
The Rs.1,450 crore IPO comprised a fresh issue of equity shares worth Rs.500 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of Rs.950 crore by promoter Dharminder Kumar Nagar and investor Commelina Ltd.
Based in Gurugram, Paras Healthcare operates a network of eight hospitals across five states and one Union Territory.

Choice Institutional Equities has initiated coverage on Paras Healthcare with a 'Buy' rating and a target price of Rs.900, implying an upside of around 30%. The brokerage has valued the company using the discounted cash flow (DCF) method, with an implied enterprise value-to-EBITDA multiple of 14 times its FY29 estimates.

The brokerage expects Paras Healthcare's revenue, EBITDA and profit after tax (PAT) to grow at compound annual growth rates (CAGRs) of 21.9%, 29.4% and 99.1%, respectively, over FY26-FY29. Its growth outlook is supported by a higher contribution from specialised, high-value healthcare services, expansion into underserved markets and operating leverage from improving occupancy and capacity utilisation.

Paras Healthcare's six core specialties - cardiac sciences, oncology, neurosciences, gastro sciences, orthopaedics and renal sciences, collectively referred to as CONGO-R - accounted for around 75% of its FY26 revenue. Choice Institutional Equities believes this focus on specialised tertiary and quaternary care, backed by advanced infrastructure, experienced clinicians and established referral networks, will support revenue growth. Improving occupancy, higher patient volumes and a greater share of complex procedures are also expected to enhance revenue productivity and strengthen earnings.

Separately, Dr Ravi Singh, Chief Research Officer at Master Capital Services, said Paras Healthcare made a positive debut on the stock market, listing at Rs.720 on both the NSE and BSE, a premium of around 3.9% over its issue price of Rs.693.

Singh highlighted the company's focus on underserved markets, where demand for quality healthcare services offers room for expansion. Its six core specialties contributed 74.7% of revenue from operations in FY26, reflecting its emphasis on specialised care.

According to Singh, India's healthcare delivery market was valued at Rs.7 lakh crore in FY25 and is estimated to have reached Rs.7.6-7.8 lakh crore in FY26. The market is projected to grow at a CAGR of 10-12% to Rs.11.2-12.2 lakh crore by FY30, with North India emerging as a key growth market. The region's healthcare delivery market is expected to reach Rs.3.6-3.8 lakh crore by FY30.

Looking ahead, Singh said investors are likely to monitor the company's ability to sustain revenue and profit growth while improving operational efficiency. Consistent growth in patient volumes, higher occupancy rates, stronger operating margins and cash flows, along with further expansion of healthcare services, could support investor interest in the stock.
